doc.brief: An invisible layout element in a `GtkConstraintLayout`.
doc.md:
An invisible layout element in a `GtkConstraintLayout`.

The `GtkConstraintLayout` treats guides like widgets. They
can be used as the source or target of a `GtkConstraint`.

Guides have a minimum, maximum and natural size. Depending
on the constraints that are applied, they can act like a
guideline that widgets can be aligned to, or like *flexible
space*.

Unlike a `GtkWidget`, a `GtkConstraintGuide` will not be drawn.

get_name.brief: Retrieves the name set using gtk_constraint_guide_set_name().
get_name.md: Retrieves the name set using gtk_constraint_guide_set_name().

get_strength.md: Retrieves the strength set using gtk_constraint_guide_set_strength().

set_max_size.md:
Sets the maximum size of `guide`.

If `guide` is attached to a `GtkConstraintLayout`,
the constraints will be updated to reflect the new size.

set_min_size.md:
Sets the minimum size of `guide`.

If `guide` is attached to a `GtkConstraintLayout`,
the constraints will be updated to reflect the new size.

set_name.brief: Sets a name for the given `GtkConstraintGuide`.
set_name.md:
Sets a name for the given `GtkConstraintGuide`.

The name is useful for debugging purposes.

set_nat_size.md:
Sets the natural size of `guide`.

If `guide` is attached to a `GtkConstraintLayout`,
the constraints will be updated to reflect the new size.

set_strength.brief: Sets the strength of the constraint on the natural size of the given `GtkConstraintGuide`.
set_strength.md:
Sets the strength of the constraint on the natural size of the
given `GtkConstraintGuide`.
